text:
Montreal comes to Boston with points in eleven straight games (8-0-3) after a 2-1 overtime loss to Minnesota on Tuesday, a game Kirill Kaprizov won in the extra frame. They're doing it without Ivan Demidov, and Cole Caufield has moved onto the first line beside Juraj Slafkovský and Zachary Bolduc has jumped to the top power-play unit. Boston has won four straight, including a 4-1 win over Florida, but we'd note the results run ahead of the chances: the Bruins are leaning on finishing and goaltending, and they're missing James Hagens.

At five on five the teams are even, each taking 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances, not just the count). Our model has Boston at 3.21 expected goals tonight and Montreal at 2.94. The Canadiens' penalty kill allows 0.86 expected goals a game against Boston's 0.72, and Montreal's 5.2 penalties a game keep giving the other side power plays. In net, projected starters Jacob Fowler (+12.1 goals saved above expected, the shots-faced measure of goaltending, this season) and Jeremy Swayman (+10.2, after +26.5 last year) are close.

Caufield is our top Montreal scorer at 36%, and as Karine Hains of The Hockey News posted Tuesday, the Habs were hoping to "spring Caufield out of the box." Pavel Zacha and David Pastrnak lead Boston's list at 30% and 34% to score. Among our under-the-radar picks, Casey Mittelstadt, a third-liner at 15:17 a night, has 2.5 expected goals in his last ten games and sits at 21% to score tonight, a player to watch.
